Proposition
[basic properties of vertical and basic horizontal fields]

Source: petersen:page-0163 ↗ def:pet-ch4-vertical-horizontal-distribution 1. ch4:4.5.1Let $V$ be a vertical vector field on $ ar M$ and $X,Y,Z$ vector fields on $M$ with basic horizontal lifts $ ar X, ar Y, ar Z$. Then:

  1. $[V, ar X]$ is vertical.

  2. $(L_V ar g)( ar X, ar Y)=D_V ar g( ar X, ar Y)=0$.

  3. $ ar g([ ar X, ar Y],V)=2 ar g( abla _{ ar Y} ar X,V)=-2 ar g( abla _{ ar X} ar Y,V)=2 ar g( abla _VY,X)$.

  4. $ abla _{ ar X} ar Y=\overline{ abla _XY}+ frac 12[ ar X, ar Y]^{\mathcal V}$.

Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch4-submersion-basic-properties \sketch Since $V$ and $ ar X$ are related to $0$ and $X$, respectively, $DF[V, ar X]=[0,X]=0$, proving (1). For (2), the bracket terms in $L_V ar g( ar X, ar Y)$ vanish by (1), while $ ar g( ar X, ar Y)=g(X,Y)\circ F$ is constant along each fiber. Applying the Koszul formula to two basic horizontal fields and one vertical field gives all identities in (3). Its vertical projection is $ frac 12[ ar X, ar Y]^{\mathcal V}$; applying Koszul to three basic fields identifies the horizontal projection with $\overline{ abla _XY}$, proving (4).

□
